thread:
marta: heads up — we just pushed the backfill eviction policy tweak to na-east and i'm seeing a sharp P95 latency bump across GPU pools. same tasks are being evicted + requeued a lot.
provisioner-bot: ALERT na-east: pool-backfill-evict-rate > 150/min, avg-evict-duration=12s, affected-pools=['g4-small','a10x-medium']
infra-sre: copying logs from the deploy:
```
 2026-03-18T14:05:12Z provisioner: starting backfill pass for pool g4-small
 2026-03-18T14:05:13Z runtime: serializing KV cache for task id=tx-8c3
 2026-03-18T14:05:14Z provisioner: evicting id=tx-8c3 due to preemption
 2026-03-18T14:05:16Z runtime: cache miss for key=prefix-9f (reason=serialization-timeout)
 2026-03-18T14:05:19Z request: retry queued, latency p95 jumped to 480ms
```

marta: @ops-oncall can you scope blast radius? is this only na-east?
ops-oncall: seeing elevated tail in na-east and na1-edge; na-west mostly fine. traffic shift to eu-west in progress (started 14:08Z) but can't fully absorb large model variants.

dbenson: my quick read — the eviction tweak bumped aggressiveness to 20% higher than intended (config delta: backfill.eviction_threshold was 0.4 -> 0.32). that reduces steady-state batch size and forces more KV cache churn.
kevin: if eviction reduces batch sizes, continuous-batcher will ramp up RPCs and serialization pressure. that explains cache serialization-timeout.

shreya: short-term mitigations: 1) revert the eviction_threshold change (safe, quick), 2) toggle runtime BATCH_PROFILE to conservative (lower concurrency), 3) enable kvcache-read-through fallback for hot prefixes.

marta: prefer non-revert first if safe? why not do (2) + (3) and monitor while we stage a rollback?
ops-oncall: we can flip batch profile in 60s via flag push to all pool managers. kvcache-read-through needs a small runtime toggle but it's staged. taking action: flipping batch profile now.
provisioner-bot: ACTION batch_profile -> conservative applied to pools: g4-small,a10x-medium at 14:11:02Z (ok).
ops-oncall: p95 dropped from 480ms -> 220ms within 45s after flip. throughput down ~8% but evictions decreasing.

marta: great. shreya can you stage kvcache-read-through toggle and prepare rollback patch for eviction_threshold? we'll need a postmortem plan if ripple continues.
shreya: staging kvcache-read-through patch to rollout in canary (na-east 10%) at 14:15Z. rollback PR ready: #2987 (eviction-policy: restore 0.4).

dbenson: also worth throttling backfill job concurrency as a medium-term follow-up. open to suggestions on a safe concurrency cap.
kevin: suggest cap=4 concurrent backfill threads per host, and add jitter to avoid synchronized evict bursts.

ops-oncall: canary kvcache toggle running: 14:15:22Z -> success on canary. planning gradual ramp 10->50->100% over 5m. will abort if evict-rate > 80/min.

infra-sre: notes for post-incident: root cause = unintended config delta in backfill eviction policy + lack of guardrail for batcher/kvcache interaction. action items: tighter config CI, run stress tests for eviction bursts, add per-pool eviction-rate alarm, and a playbook step to flip to conservative batch profile.

marta: thanks team. current status — p95 back to ~210ms, evict-rate trending down. leaving this thread open while we finish the kvcache ramp and follow-ups. cc @shreya @dbenson for remediation ops. :thumbsup:
